learningObjective: Explain why TVM (and its Ansor/AutoTVM descendants) rely on real hardware measurement rather than a pure analytical cost model to select schedules.

canonicalClaims.claim: TVM's schedule search calls real hardware measurement (or a learned cost model trained on measurements) rather than a purely analytical performance model, because the effective performance of a schedule on a modern accelerator depends on many implementation-specific factors (cache behaviors, coalescing, register allocation, instruction mix, autotuner-selected block sizes) that are hard to capture in a closed-form analytical model.
conditions: The target is a modern GPU or CPU with complex microarchitecture.
The schedule space is large enough that analytical ranking would produce many false optima.
nonImplications: Does not imply that analytical models are useless; TVM uses them (or ML surrogates) to prune before measurement.
Does not imply that measurement is free — TVM's cost is dominated by autotuning time, which is a well-known trade-off.

sourceMappings.locator: §4–§5 schedule search + learned cost model motivation
§3 discussion of why measurement is necessary

misconceptions.claim: TVM uses measurement because analytical models are theoretically incorrect; a sufficiently detailed analytical model could always replace measurement.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The paper's argument is empirical: modern hardware has too many hard-to-model effects for practical closed-form models; it does not claim measurement is theoretically indispensable.

misconceptions.claim: TVM's use of measurement means it does not use any cost model at all; every schedule is executed on the target device.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TVM (and Ansor) train a learned cost model on measurements and use it to rank / prune candidates so that only promising ones are measured.

misconceptions.claim: TVM's measurement approach is only used for GPUs; on CPUs the schedule can always be chosen by an analytical roofline argument.
misconceptions.whyWrong: CPUs likewise expose complex microarchitectural effects (SIMD vs scalar, cache blocking, false sharing) that TVM/Ansor tune via measurement-driven search.
